\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بحران} (buhrān)}{بحران (buhrān)}]{\ur{بحران} (buhrān) — a crisis}

\label{lesson:UR-C371-buhran}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to smash, then the Urdu for to squash.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بحران}}
\textbf{\ur{بحران}} — \emph{buhrān} — \textquotedblleft{}a crisis\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{بارش} \ur{نہیں} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{پانی} \ur{کا} \ur{بحران} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar bārish nahīṅ huī to pānī kā buhrān ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it does not rain, there will be a water crisis.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بحران}} (\emph{buhrān}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{buḥrān}, \textquotedblleft{}the crisis of a fever\textquotedblright{}, the turning point of an illness.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{buhrān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{buhrān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar bārish nahīṅ huī to pānī kā buhrān ho gā.} — If it does not rain, there will be a water crisis.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to smash, then the Urdu for to squash, then say \emph{buhrān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بحران} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A crisis\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جان} \ur{لیوا} (jān-levā)}{جان لیوا (jān-levā)}]{\ur{جان} \ur{لیوا} (jān-levā) — deadly; fatal}

\label{lesson:UR-C371-jan-leva}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a crisis, then the Urdu for poison.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جان} \ur{لیوا}}
\textbf{\ur{جان} \ur{لیوا}} — \emph{jān-levā} — \textquotedblleft{}deadly; fatal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{یہ} \ur{زہر} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{جان} \ur{لیوا} \ur{ہو} \ur{سکتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar yih zahr hai to jān-levā ho saktā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If this is poison, it could be deadly.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جان} \ur{لیوا}} (\emph{jān-levā}) is built from \emph{jān}, \textquotedblleft{}life\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Persian \emph{jān}, \textquotedblleft{}life, soul\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{levā}, \textquotedblleft{}taking\textquotedblright{}, made on \textbf{\ur{لینا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{}. Life-taking.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رسنا} (risnā)}{رسنا (risnā)}]{\ur{رسنا} (risnā) — to seep; to leak (of a liquid)}

\label{lesson:UR-C371-risna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for poison, then the Urdu for deadly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رسنا}}
\textbf{\ur{رسنا}} — \emph{risnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to seep; to leak (of a liquid)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{چھت} \ur{سے} \ur{پانی} \ur{رسا} \ur{تو} \ur{کمرہ} \ur{گیلا} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar chhat se pānī risā to kamrā gīlā ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If water seeps through the roof, the room will get wet.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{پانی} \ur{دیوار} \ur{سے} \ur{رسا}, \emph{voh pānī dīvār se risā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رسنا}} (\emph{risnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{risnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to leak out, to drip\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*riśyate}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 10745).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{risnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{risnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar chhat se pānī risā to kamrā gīlā ho gā.} — If water seeps through the roof, the room will get wet.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for poison, then the Urdu for deadly, then say \emph{risnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{رسنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To seep; to leak (of a liquid)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پھٹنا} (phaṭnā)}{پھٹنا (phaṭnā)}]{\ur{پھٹنا} (phaṭnā) — to split open; to burst}

\label{lesson:UR-C371-phatna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for deadly, then the Urdu for to seep.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پھٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پھٹنا}} — \emph{phaṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to split open; to burst\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{پائپ} \ur{پھٹا} \ur{تو} \ur{گھر} \ur{میں} \ur{پانی} \ur{آئے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar pāip phaṭā to ghar meṅ pānī āe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the pipe bursts, water will get into the house.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{پائپ} \ur{پھٹ} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh pāip phaṭ gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پھٹنا}} (\emph{phaṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{phāṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be split\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{sphāṭayati}, \textquotedblleft{}causes to split\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13825).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}
